page: Amazon Web Services m8gd.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It is powered by an ARMv9-based AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processor operating at 2.8 GHz. The instance features 4 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, providing 4 vCPUs. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance includes a bundled 237 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate solid general-purpose capabilities. In single-core and multi-core processing, the instance achieves average tier results, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1858.0 and a multi-core score of 5852.0. Memory bandwidth is robust, reaching 462.07 GB/sec for small block cached reads and 96.47 GB/sec for large block uncached reads. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression performs in the top 25% tier at 14.26 GB/sec. However, the instance exhibits weaker performance in Passmark CPU tests, particularly in encryption benchmarks where it scores in the bottom 10%, likely due to the lack of specific hardware acceleration flags beyond standard AES.

The m8gd.xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency by combining dedicated ARM64 compute resources with integrated high-speed NVMe local storage, reducing the need for external block storage for temporary data. This hardware profile is well-suited for general-purpose applications, static web serving, Redis key-value stores, and database operations. It is less optimal for intensive cryptographic tasks or large-scale LLM inference, where text generation speeds for a 7B model drop to 6.54 tokens per second.
description: Amazon Web Services m8gd.xlarge is a general-purpose, ARM64-based instance powered by a 2.8 GHz AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processor. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, it provides 4 dedicated physical cores and 16.0 GB of system memory. The instance features a bundled 237 GB NVMe SSD local instance store and a baseline network speed of 2 Gbps. Benchmark results place its compute and memory performance in the average tier, highlighted by a strong single-threaded bzip3 decompression speed of 14.26 GB/sec and a Redis throughput of 9.34 million SET operations per second. However, it shows weaker results in encryption and LLM inference tasks. This instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring local scratch space, making it suitable for static web serving, database operations, caching layers, and general-purpose application hosting.
